code_first.q: Predict the number of bytes in 40 bits.
p: Extend to print the remaining bits using MOD.
code_first.a: Prints 5; with 64 bits prints 8; remainder is bits MOD 8.

previous_learning_exam.q: A school needs a high-capacity, low-cost backup drive for files accessed infrequently. Identify suitable storage and justify two characteristics. [3]
previous_learning_exam.a: Magnetic HDD [1]: typically lower cost per GB [1] and large available capacities [1], suitable where frequent fast access is not a priority.

A device has 6 GB free. Each file uses 750 MB. Calculate the maximum whole files it can store. [3]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.
6 GB = 6000 MB [1]; 6000 ÷ 750 [1] = 8 whole files [1], ignoring overhead.

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: There are eight bits per byte. DIV gives the number of complete bytes.

stretch.task: Change bits to 41 and extend Code First to print the whole bytes and leftover bits using DIV and MOD.
stretch.hint: Use bits DIV 8 and bits MOD 8 as separate calculations.
stretch.answer: 41 DIV 8 = 5 whole bytes; 41 MOD 8 = 1 remaining bit.

mastery.task: Write code to calculate how many complete 250 MB files fit into a device with 2.6 GB available, using decimal conversion. Print both the whole-file count and unused MB.
mastery.hint: First convert 2.6 GB to 2600 MB. Then use DIV and MOD with 250.
mastery.answer: capacityMB = 2.6 * 1000; files = capacityMB DIV 250; spareMB = capacityMB MOD 250; print(files); print(spareMB). Result: 10 complete files and 100 MB spare, assuming no storage overhead.
